title: perf(servicelb): release the aya object after attach so the DaemonSet idles thin
description:
Pin the maps, drop the aya Ebpf object after attach, trim the heap, and
reopen maps from their pins when they are next needed, so the DaemonSet
container idles thin instead of holding load-time state forever.

The blocking loop at src/main.rs:204 is correct and must stay. A DaemonSet
Pod only accepts restartPolicy Always, so exiting would be restarted and
eventually backed off. The cost is not the sleep, it is what the process
holds while sleeping. Ebpf::load parses the object at line 153 and keeps the
BTF, relocation state, and program registry alive for the whole process
lifetime, and the 214 KiB embedded blob is resident once touched. Glibc does
not return that heap on its own, so resident memory sits at the load-time
high-water mark, which in a container is what the memory request has to cover
on every node.

MapData::from_pin exists in aya 0.14 for reopening. Phase 5's watcher needs
map handles, not the parsed ELF.

Worth recording while here: since Linux 5.11, BPF map memory is charged to
the creating process's cgroup, so the roughly 1.82 MiB of map memory counts
against this container's own memory limit rather than sitting outside it. Map
sizing and container limits are one budget, not two. The bump_memlock_rlimit
call at src/main.rs:296 only matters for kernels older than that.

DONE WHEN: steady-state RSS in the existing loader-rss.csv sampler drops
measurably below the load-time peak, with the attachment still live.
close_reason: PR #13 opened. Steady-state RSS 19936-19940 KB (baseline) -> 19840-19860 KB (fixed), consistent ~90KB/0.45% drop, non-overlapping across 7 runs on beep-node-b; scripts/smoke.sh --vm beep-node-b PASS confirms attachment survives the Ebpf drop.

title: perf(servicelb): make the per-packet flow-table writes conditional
description:
Replace the unconditional per-packet map inserts with
lookup-then-write-on-miss.

servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:238 inserts into FWD_FLOW on every forwarded
packet, and line 418 inserts into REV_FLOW on every decapped packet, not just
on the first packet of a flow. An LRU hash update takes the bucket
raw_spinlock and can run the LRU shrink path. A lookup is an RCU read that
already refreshes the entry's LRU reference bit, so recency is preserved
without the write. The difference is largest under multi-core load, where
several CPUs serialize on one bucket lock for a single busy flow.

FWD_FLOW's value is constant per flow, so skipping the rewrite is trivially
safe. REV_FLOW's value can legitimately change if the ingress node changes,
so the check there is exists-and-matches rather than plain existence.

DONE WHEN: steady-state packets of an established flow take the read path,
verified by a map-update counter that stays flat while traffic flows.
close_reason: PR #14 opened

title: perf(servicelb): gate the egress conntrack lookup on POD_TARGETS membership
description:
Gate the uplink-egress conntrack lookup on POD_TARGETS membership, checking
only that the source address is a backend Pod on this node and deliberately
not comparing the port.

try_uplink_egress_return at servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:537 performs a
40-byte-key LRU hash lookup on every TCP and UDP packet leaving the node
before it can reject non-ServiceLB traffic. POD_TARGETS is a 32-entry map
with a 4-byte key, so probing it first is a far cheaper hash and it
short-circuits before the 37-byte key is even built on the stack.

Membership only, not a port match. Comparing the packet's source port against
the current POD_TARGETS value would couple the return path to a value that
can change under it during a rolling update or a targetPort change, dropping
live flows whose reverse entry was written under the old port. The current
code cannot produce that failure, because it matches purely on the stored
tuple. Membership is safe by construction: a flow only has a reverse entry if
the forward path found its pod in this map, so anything still live passes,
and a pod absent from the map is going away regardless.

Pairs with the REV_FLOW-miss bead, which needs exactly this positive
identification before it can safely turn a miss into a drop.

DONE WHEN: traffic not sourced from a backend Pod rejects without touching
the conntrack table, and a test covers that a targetPort change does not
break an in-flight flow.
close_reason: PR #1624 opened

title: perf(servicelb): direct packet access instead of bpf_skb_load_bytes on both uplink hooks
description:
Replace ctx.load with direct packet access on both uplink hooks, because
every ctx.load is a bpf_skb_load_bytes helper call and these hooks see all
node traffic, not just ServiceLB's.

Confirmed in aya-ebpf 0.2.1: TcContext::load delegates to SkBuff::load, which
calls bpf_skb_load_bytes. Cost per packet before either hook can even reject
non-ServiceLB traffic:

- try_uplink_egress_return, servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:537. Seven helper
  calls plus a 40-byte-key LRU hash lookup.
- try_uplink_ingress, servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:207. Five helper calls plus
  a VIP_MAP lookup.

That is paid by kubelet, etcd, image pulls, flannel, and everything else
entering or leaving the node. ctx.data and ctx.data_end are available in this
aya version, turning each read into a plain load behind one bounds check.
Adjacent fields can also coalesce: the source and destination addresses are
contiguous, as are the two ports.

Caution: direct packet access covers the linear head only. Headers are linear
in practice for tc ingress and for egress from a local socket, but any read
that reaches into a payload, which native QUIC will need for the DCID,
requires bpf_skb_pull_data or a load-bytes fallback.

This gets more valuable under the dual-stack and QUIC requirements, not less.
IPv6 means branching on ethertype with different header offsets and walking
extension headers, each of which is another helper call under the current
approach.

DONE WHEN: header reads go through ctx.data and ctx.data_end with
verifier-accepted bounds checks, and the servicelb smoke fixture still passes
end to end.
close_reason: PR #15 opened

title: docs(ebpf-lb): correct the VIP-space vs pod-CIDR disjointness claim
description:
The claim that VIP-space and the pod CIDR are disjoint by construction is
false for hostNetwork Pods, and the doc uses it to justify a design choice.

ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md line 89 states the two ranges never
collide and concludes that one map per protocol can cover both the forward
and reverse roles. A Pod with hostNetwork true has a pod IP equal to its node
IP, which is exactly VIP space under the node-owned-address model. That is
standard Kubernetes semantics, not misconfiguration, and this repo already
ships two hostNetwork DaemonSets in manifests/kube-proxy.yaml and
manifests/flannel.yaml. The doc specifies the servicelb control plane itself
as hostNetwork at line 131.

Concrete collision, node N at 192.168.109.3. A forward key for a service
fronted at N holds N's address in its other-address slot. A reverse key for a
hostNetwork backend on N holds the same address in the same slot. A client
legally reusing one local port across both makes the two 37-byte keys
byte-identical.

The ranges are also only disjoint by configuration today, not by
construction. The pod CIDR is 10.244.0.0/16 from scripts/install.sh:890 and
node addresses sit on 192.168.x.x, set by unrelated mechanisms with no
cross-validation. The --vip-ip flag at src/main.rs:56 is an unvalidated
address with no check that it is the node's own or outside the pod CIDR.

Calibration note: the same paragraph of this doc was already wrong once,
specifying LRU_PERCPU_HASH, which was empirically disproved and corrected.
That is reason to audit the neighbouring sentence rather than defer to it.

Consider merging with aie31.3, which corrects the map type and footprint in
the same file. Kept separate here because this one also needs a code change.

DONE WHEN: the doc states the real constraint rather than a false invariant,
and the loader rejects a VIP that falls inside the pod CIDR.
close_reason: Doc correction landed in PR #1614; loader-side validation (also required by this bead's done-when) is out of scope for this doc-only PR and tracked separately as mayor-aie31.24

title: net/servicelb: userspace controller -- watch type=LoadBalancer Services + EndpointSlice, program dataplane maps
description:
Phase 5 of mayor-aie31 (ServiceLB implementation epic). Per-node
userspace control plane per ai/extended-context/ebpf-lb-dataplane.md's
"Userspace control plane" section: one DaemonSet per node, hostNetwork
plus CAP_BPF/CAP_NET_ADMIN, no CRI socket. Loads and pins the Phase 1
through 3 tc-bpf programs once, then watches Service (type=LoadBalancer)
and EndpointSlice via u7s's existing watch machinery (reuse, do not
reimplement), and on change writes the VIP map, the endpoint map, and the
backend-local vni_to_pod map -- then idles. No persistent proxy loop; the
kernel does the packet forwarding (mirrors klipper-lb's memory-discipline
model, per cni-svclb-landscape.md).

Extract the Service/EndpointSlice-diff-to-map-entries logic into a pure
Rust function, separate from the async watch-handler plumbing, so it is
directly unit-testable (Rule 14) without a live cluster.

Depends on Phase 4 (mayor-lrbvo) passing -- do not invest in the full
controller ahead of the go/no-go gate; if gate 1 or 2 fails, the map
schema or hook design this controller programs may need to change first.
Blocks Phase 6 (kube-proxy/flannel coexistence verification) -- proving
coexistence needs a controller-driven system running real Service
objects, not Phase 2's static test fixture.

Risk: MEDIUM -- lower than the dataplane phases since this reuses
existing watch code per the mechanism doc, but wrong map population
(stale entries, missed EndpointSlice updates, VNI allocation bugs) is a
silent-wrong-routing failure mode, not a crash.

Verification: unit tests for the pure reconcile function (Service/
EndpointSlice fixtures in, expected map-entry diffs out, including add/
update/delete and multi-EndpointSlice-per-Service cases). Integration
test on a Lima cluster: create/update/delete a real type=LoadBalancer
Service and confirm map contents via bpftool map dump match.

title: design(servicelb): aie31.21 eviction ignores cross-node convergence drift - delivery node must be the authoritative consistency point
description: Operator raised 2026-09-07: the aie31.21 affinity+eviction doc reasons about eviction as a per-node reconcile but never addresses the cross-node convergence WINDOW. Each node's DaemonSet processes the same EndpointSlice event at different times (uplink latency), so node eBPF state can drift apart for multiple seconds before converging. Governing principle to add to the doc: dataplane is eventually-consistent per node; correctness must NOT depend on synchronized updates; worst case during the window must be bounded transient drop/hang, NEVER misdelivery to a wrong live pod. Scenarios: new-flow selection divergence = safe (per-flow ECMP-sticky to one ingress node); stale FWD_FLOW pin during removal lag = blackhole/hang if IP not reused (bounded, ok) BUT misdelivery if the departed pod's IP is reused before the lagging ingress node evicts (UNSAFE - the drift window widens this). RESOLVING INVARIANT: make the delivery (backend-host) node validate each inbound Geneve-decap packet against its OWN current serving-set for the front IP before delivering - the host has a lag-free view of its local pods, so ingress drift degrades to a drop at the authoritative node, not a cross-service leak. OPEN QUESTION to verify against code: does the inbound decap-forward delivery path in crates/servicelb/servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs currently do this membership check? aie31.14 gates EGRESS on POD_TARGETS (different hook) - may not cover inbound delivery. Action: amend aie31.21 doc with the cross-node-drift section + invariant; file a build bead if the delivery-side validation is missing. Part of parked aie31 epic.
notes: Verdict: invariant does NOT hold today. try_geneve_decap_forward (servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:331-471) trusts the ingress-stamped Geneve pod_ip unconditionally and DNATs to it; its only check, TARGET_PORTS.get(front tuple) (main.rs:361-368), validates "this node serves some backend for this front", not "this pod_ip is a current member" -- no analogue of aie31.14's egress POD_TARGETS-membership gate exists on the inbound decap-delivery path. Drift verdict: new-flow divergence is SAFE (per-flow ECMP-sticky); stale FWD_FLOW pin without IP reuse is SAFE (bounded blackhole/hang); stale pin WITH pod-IP reuse before the lagging ingress evicts is UNSAFE -- misdelivers to the new pod, and the drift window directly widens this exposure. Doc amended: ai/findings/2026-09-06-mayor-aie31.21-affinity-pinning-eviction.md, new "Cross-node convergence & drift" section (keeps its aie31.21 header, doc-only PR under mayor-1dwwz). Build follow-on filed: mayor-tavxy (P2, parent aie31, cross-refs aie31.21 + aie31.14). Left OPEN per dispatch instructions -- operator resolves aie31.21 separately.
close_reason: Deliverable verifiably done: cross-node convergence-drift invariant documented (aie31.21 doc drift section) and the build-side fix landed as mayor-tavxy / PR #11 (decap-delivery validates target pod against local serving-set). Remaining aie31.21 affinity/eviction coupling is tracked in aie31.21 itself; no separate open work here.

title: servicelb-ebpf: dual-role node's ungated reverse writes can LRU-evict a forward entry from the shared FLOW_TABLE
description: Accepted residual of aie31.17's flow-table merge (PR #10), flagged by the reviewer as needing its own bead. FWD_PENDING stays a separate admission-gated tier, but merging FWD_MAIN+REV_FLOW into one FLOW_TABLE means the reverse role -- which has NO admission gate -- shares capacity with forward entries. On a DUAL-ROLE node (ingress AND backend), a large reverse-write burst could LRU-evict a forward (admission-gated) entry. Failure mode is AVAILABILITY (the forward flow re-mints), NOT misdelivery. Reviewer + operator ACCEPTED shipping without a gate because: it's honestly documented (ebpf/src/main.rs:269-270 + design doc + PR #10 body), unreachable by current smoke fixtures (the anti-flush flood never completes a forward-decap, so never produces reverse-tagged writes), and triggering it needs overlay-internal positioning (a materially higher bar than the off-path spoofing the FWD_PENDING split defended). REVISIT with a reverse-side admission gate or per-direction capacity split IF dual-role nodes become a real deployment target. Ref: PR #10 review pullrequestreview-5152918958.
notes:
Re-anchor (2026-09-10, post #10/#14): STILL-HOLDS but it is a DOCUMENTED, DELIBERATELY-ACCEPTED trade-off, not an undiscovered bug. Reverse-tagged FLOW_TABLE writes (ebpf/src/main.rs:807-810) are ungated (write on first backend-decap, no admission gate); forward entries (:906-914) ARE gated (require return-leg promotion). On a dual-role node the shared 16384-entry LRU means a reverse-write burst can LRU-evict an established forward entry -- impossible pre-#10 when FWD_MAIN/REV_FLOW were separate maps; #14 PortMemo (3rd slot) slightly worsens occupancy. FAILURE MODE = availability (evicted flow re-mints on next packet), NOT misdelivery/correctness. Explicitly documented + accepted in the FLOW_TABLE comment (:275-310) and PR #10 review (pullrequestreview-5152918958) as a large-burst-only, dual-role-only concern. Fix options: A) gate reverse writes behind admission (per-packet cost, risks dropping legit return traffic); B) partition table by direction tag; C) per-direction sizing knob (mirror --fwd-pending-max-entries); D) status quo (what #10 chose). RECOMMENDATION: DEFER unless dual-role deployments become a near-term target -- availability-not-correctness, rare, already documented, and the fix is not free.
DECISION (operator 2026-09-10): ACCEPT the tradeoff; defer the code-side fix (reverse-write admission gate / partition / separate-maps) until it causes ACTUAL data loss. Rationale: availability-only (evicted forward flow re-mints on next packet, never misdelivery), dual-role node + large-burst only. Follow-on: load-test to find + document the safe concurrent-outgoing-flow burst threshold as a known operational limit (filed separately).

title: test-rig: eth0/user-v2-ingress cross-node smoke -- host client -> node-a VIP -> geneve-over-wg0 -> node-b backend
description:
GOAL: a 2-node smoke variant where the client arrives on node-a's ETHERNET (user-v2/Lima NIC) ingress -- NOT on wg0 -- and beep encapsulates over wg0 as the cross-node transport to node-b. Topology: host client -> (Lima port-forward) -> node-a user-v2 VIP:port -> beep tc-bpf ingress (uplink-iface = the user-v2 NIC, e.g. eth0/lima0, confirm inside the VM) -> bpf_redirect into geneve0 -> geneve OUTER packet routes to node-b over the wg0 underlay -> node-b decaps -> backend (nc -l serving 'OK') responds -> round trip back to the host client.

WHY: (1) more realistic than the existing wg-2node rig, where node-b doubles as its own client and the ingress uplink is wg0 (10.99.0.2:19100). Here the client is a real external origin (the macOS host via a Lima port-forward to node-a's VIP) and the backend is a genuinely separate node. (2) This is the multi-KIND path from beep-eix (eth0-in, wg0-out) -- exercises it as a TEST even before full multi-interface support, since single-interface eth0-ingress already works. (3) It is INDEPENDENT of the f3ru5 blocker: f3ru5 is the wg0-AS-INGRESS L3 redirect drop; here ingress is Ethernet (mac_len=14) so the redirect-into-geneve0 works. => testable NOW, before f3ru5 lands.

SETUP (sketch, adapt from scripts/smoke-wg-2node.sh + smoke-wg-2node-remote.sh): keep the wg0 tunnel + geneve0 collect-metadata setup between node-a/node-b; change node-a's beep --uplink-iface to the user-v2 NIC (was wg0); expose node-a's VIP to the host via a Lima port-forward (lima/beep.yaml or 'limactl forward'); drive the client with curl from the macOS host instead of from node-b's root netns; assert body 'OK' + dump geneve0/wg0 counters + bpftool map dumps on failure (same evidence as the existing rig).

CAVEAT: this sidesteps f3ru5 on the FORWARD INGRESS leg only. The RETURN leg (node-b -> node-a -> client) may surface its own L3/mac_len issue depending on how the reverse path egresses -- characterize it, don't assume full green. Reachability confirmed feasible: lima user-v2 gives VMs host-unroutable IPs, but a port-forward to node-a's VIP is a legitimate external-client stand-in (delivers to the Ethernet ingress; does NOT bypass the wg0 transport).

XREF: beep-eix (multi-interface feature this tests), mayor-f3ru5 (wg0-ingress path this is independent of), existing scripts/smoke-wg-2node.sh (wg0-ingress rig to adapt from).
design: P3, near-term testable (independent of f3ru5). A distinct rig from the wg0-ingress smoke, not a replacement. Value: realistic external-client + separate-backend topology; exercises the eth0-in/wg0-out multi-KIND path.
acceptance_criteria: A host-originated request to node-a's user-v2 VIP completes a cross-node round trip (geneve encap over the wg0 underlay, node-b backend responds 'OK') and the rig asserts it; on failure it dumps geneve0/wg0 counters + VIP/conntrack map dumps. Forward-ingress leg proven; return-leg behavior characterized (pass or documented blocker).
notes:
FINDING (rig built, PR #20): forward leg NOT proven end-to-end -- structural blocker, not a rig bug, so bead stays OPEN per dispatch brief.

Mechanism proven: VERIFIER-ACCEPT on both nodes (--uplink-iface eth0 confirmed as node-a's real Lima user-v2 NIC), FWD_PENDING minted on node-a for the client SYN, geneve0 TX/RX packet counts match exactly node-a->node-b, node-b's decap+DNAT writes the correct reverse conntrack entry.

Blocker: with only 2 assigned VMs and node-b required to host the backend, the client is necessarily node-b's own root netns (same reason smoke-wg-2node uses this convention -- a synthetic/foreign client address does not survive Lima's user-v2 virtual switch, confirmed via a standalone veth+forwarding test). `ip route get <node-b's own address>` on node-b unconditionally resolves to `local ... dev lo` -- the kernel can never select the Geneve-transport uplink (wg0) as the return leg's egress device for a destination that is the node's own address, regardless of eBPF logic or sysctl changes. Confirmed via /proc/net/snmp (TCP PassiveOpens on node-b never increments) and trace-cmd (decap'd packet dropped at tcp_v4_rcv+0x98 reason: NO_SOCKET).

Same class of problem as beep-n24 (client co-located with backend node), for the wg0-ingress rig -- this investigation additionally establishes WHY it's structural (the local-route short-circuit) rather than just a martian-source/sysctl issue. Real fix needs a 3rd VM (client address genuinely foreign to node-b), out of this bead's assigned 2-VM scope.

Also ruled out (investigated, evidenced): a literal macOS-host client via Lima port-forward. Lima's automatic port-forward dials the guest's OWN loopback address from inside the guest netns (never reaches eth0 tc-ingress); `limactl tunnel`'s SOCKS bridge accepts the CONNECT but delivers zero bytes/packets to the target's eth0.

RE-VERIFIED (2026-09-10, PR #20 branch worker/agent-afce641d5eacf8caa, live re-run on beep-node-a/b): NOT a rig-config bug and NOT a dataplane DNAT bug -- the already-documented structural client-colocation blocker, confirmed with fresh evidence, plus one correction to the earlier characterization.

Three data points line up exactly (no rig misconfiguration):
- geneve0 capture (pre-eBPF-DNAT, kernel Geneve decap only): inner SYN src=192.168.104.14:45980 dst=192.168.104.13:19100 (still the VIP, as expected before the tc hook runs).
- VIP_MAP/TARGET_PORTS/POD_TARGETS dumps on node-b: front 192.168.104.13:19100/tcp -> backend_node_ip 10.99.0.4, pod_ip 198.51.100.60, target_port 18090 -- all correct.
- `ss -tlnp`: nc alive, LISTEN on 198.51.100.60:18090 (TCP/IPv4) -- matches target_port exactly.

CORRECTION to the "forward SYN dropped NO_SOCKET" phrasing: lo capture during a fresh repro shows nc's OWN kernel emitting a genuine SYN-ACK from 198.51.100.60:18090, proving the decap'd+DNAT'd forward SYN DOES reach nc's real LISTEN socket (a NO_SOCKET drop cannot produce a SYN-ACK). A parallel trace-cmd -e skb:kfree_skb capture across a repeat attempt recorded zero kfree_skb events -- no NO_SOCKET drop fired this run. What actually breaks is the SYN-ACK's return: since its dst (192.168.104.14:45980) is node-b's own address, the kernel's local route sends it back via `lo` instead of wg0/geneve0, where it arrives with src=198.51.100.60:18090 -- not a match for curl's SYN-SENT socket (which expects a reply from 192.168.104.13:19100) -- so node-b's own stack RSTs it immediately. Same root cause the existing notes already named (client-colocation local-route short-circuit), just pinned to the exact packet that dies.

Verdict: no fix applied, none needed -- this is the environmental 2-VM-topology limit already on record, not a regression. Real fix still needs a 3rd VM. Bead stays OPEN/scope-blocked as before.

title: feat(loader+ebpf): support multiple uplink + relay interfaces (not a single --uplink-iface)
description:
GOAL: beep must support MULTIPLE interfaces, not the single --uplink-iface it has today. Example node: eth0 (public internet) + wg0 (WireGuard) + eth1 (VPC-local). 'External' clients can arrive on eth0 OR wg0, and return/relay traffic may need to egress over eth1 OR wg0. Two dimensions: (a) multiple INGRESS uplinks admitting client traffic; (b) multiple EGRESS/relay interfaces for the outbound leg (new -- today the return path is single-uplink).

CURRENT SINGLE-INTERFACE LIMITS (interface audit over PR#3-era code):
- src/main.rs:76-82 -- --uplink-iface + --geneve-iface are single-valued String (default eth0/geneve0), NOT repeatable.
- src/main.rs:331-356 -- attach loop hardcodes 3 tc-bpf hooks all on the ONE uplink + geneve iface.
- src/main.rs:277-284 & ebpf/src/main.rs:253-263 -- Config holds a SINGLE uplink_ifindex + SINGLE uplink_l2_hlen, written once at load (src/main.rs:372-396); every eBPF redirect (ebpf/src/main.rs:283,644,737) reads that single value.

STRUCTURAL CHANGES (scope sketch, not final design):
- Repeatable --uplink-iface + a way to designate relay/egress interface(s).
- Config redesign: multiple ifindices with a PER-INTERFACE uplink_l2_hlen -- critical, since eth0 is L2/Ethernet (hlen=14) and wg0 is L3-only (hlen=0); they cannot share one value.
- Attach loop over N uplinks.
- eBPF redirect logic keyed on the INCOMING interface (currently assumes one), plus egress-interface SELECTION for the relay leg.

RELATIONSHIP: the wg0-uplink path must work end-to-end first (blocker mayor-f3ru5: L3-only wg0 -> Ethernet-type geneve0 redirect drops in-kernel; leading BPF_ADJ_ROOM_MAC fix DISPROVEN 2026-09-09). Multi-interface is broader/orthogonal, but any wg0 case inherits f3ru5. Not a hard dep.
design: Operator decision 2026-09-09: FUTURE feature, P3, not a blocker to anything now -- bump only if it becomes a blocker later. Subtlety to preserve: per-interface L2 header length (Ethernet 14 vs L3-only 0) must be per-uplink, not a single Config field.
acceptance_criteria: Loader accepts >1 uplink and >=1 designated relay/egress interface; Config carries per-interface ifindex+l2_hlen; tc-bpf hooks attach across all uplinks; eBPF admits client traffic on any configured uplink and selects the correct egress interface for the relay leg; single-uplink behavior unchanged as a subset.
notes:
SCOPE CLARIFICATION (operator 2026-09-09): this bead is COUNT, not KIND. It covers supporting MULTIPLE interfaces SIMULTANEOUSLY -- repeatable --uplink-iface, attach loop over N uplinks, Config with multiple ifindices, redirect keyed on the incoming iface, egress-iface selection. It is DISTINCT from supporting multiple KINDS of interface (L2 Ethernet hlen=14 vs L3-only like wg0 hlen=0), which is needed even for a SINGLE-interface / single-node bind and is delivered by mayor-f3ru5 (make an L3-only wg0 uplink work at all: synthesize a 14-byte L2 header via bpf_skb_change_head, gated on l2_hlen==0). f3ru5 is the PREREQUISITE that makes per-interface l2_hlen meaningful; beep-eix adds the many-at-once orchestration on top. Do not conflate KIND (f3ru5, even single-interface) with COUNT (this bead).
Cross-node-test relevance (operator 2026-09-10): once multi-uplink lands (eth0 ingress + wg0 transport simultaneously), the macOS HOST can be the cross-node test client via eth0 -- an alternative to the 3rd VM (beep-vuh) for the client-address-non-local-to-backend requirement. title: net/servicelb: decide eBPF tc-bpf hook topology accounting for future TPROXY return-leg reuse -- single hook vs separate hooks, kernel perf and memory
description: L3 hook-topology design decision for the eBPF ServiceLB dataplane. title: design(servicelb): CID-based QUIC keying needs cluster-wide server_id-to-endpoint distribution, not just a per-node map
description: Operator raised 2026-09-07 on g3lag: the server-id-encoded CID (QUIC-LB draft) path the doc treats as a later opt-in has an un-spelled-out cross-node cost. Each node runs its own eBPF with its own map, so a per-node CID map cannot route a client that reconnects/migrates onto a DIFFERENT node. For server-id CID routing to work cluster-wide, EVERY node's eBPF needs (a) the shared CID-decode config (QUIC-LB encoding key/params, rotated in lockstep) and (b) a replicated server_id-to-backend-location table; a node lacking either cannot decode/route the CID. Operator's proposed mechanism (CONFIRMED correct + necessary): the cooperative L7 LB/backend allocates a persistent server_id per endpoint and publishes it via a CRD (or EndpointSlice/Pod annotation, or dedicated channel) that every node's userspace controller watches and programs into its eBPF map -- same distribution pattern as today's VIP/endpoint maps, keyed on server_id. UPSIDE worth recording: this scheme SOLVES cross-node reconnection/migration affinity that per-node conntrack FWD_FLOW pins fundamentally cannot (routing target travels in the CID, so any node decodes-and-routes statelessly; conntrack pins are node-local and break on cross-node reconnect). COST (reinforces g3lag's pass-through-now recommendation): threefold -- backend cooperation (only Envoy generates QUIC-LB CIDs today), shared+rotated decode secret across all nodes, and cluster-wide server_id-to-endpoint distribution. 4-tuple pass-through needs none of it, accepting only affinity-breaks-on-QUIC-migration. Coupling: same per-node convergence lag as 1dwwz drift, but smaller surface (per-endpoint-churn, not per-flow); tavxy delivery-node validation still bounds worst case to a drop. Action: fold into the g3lag findings doc's CID-based-later cost section; no code. Part of parked aie31 epic.
notes: RESEARCH RESULT (2026-09-07): Envoy does NOT publish a discoverable server_id-per-endpoint CRD. server_id is STATIC config (config.core.v3.DataSource: inline/file/env var; AWS EKS's NLB controller injects AWS_LBC_QUIC_SERVER_ID as a per-pod env var Envoy reads at startup). No xDS, no k8s resource surfaces the mapping. QUIC-LB draft explicitly puts parameter distribution OUT OF SCOPE (out-of-band). Envoy Gateway / Istio / Gateway API do not expose server_id. IMPLICATION: u7s must OWN the server_id distribution -- cannot observe an existing Envoy resource. Model: (1) u7s assigns the server_id space to nodes/endpoints, (2) publishes its OWN CRD/ConfigMap that its per-node eBPF watches for server_id->{backend}, (3) injects the IDs into Envoy (or the NLB controller does, on AWS). Net: CID-based keying requires u7s to BUILD+OWN an assignment+distribution+injection subsystem -- MORE machinery than 'observe Envoy', further reinforcing g3lag's pass-through-now recommendation. Refs: envoyproxy.io quic_lb.proto; quicwg.org load-balancers draft; aws-load-balancer-controller QUIC guide.

description: Surfaced live by mayor-ek41c (PR #1525). title: servicelb-ebpf: backend src-port remap re-derives every packet -> LRU eviction reassigns port mid-connection
description: From #1567 pa0ze round-3 critical review (MED, review 5115377623, confirmed by execution). resolve_backend_src_port (crates/servicelb/servicelb-common/src/lib.rs ~165) re-derives the synthetic backend src-port from the same deterministic seed on EVERY packet with no persisted decision. If an LRU eviction removes an UNRELATED occupant at an earlier probe index between two packets of the same flow, the flow re-probes, finds that earlier slot now free, and commits a DIFFERENT port mid-connection -> reverse-path breakage. Only manifests under map-full LRU eviction pressure (conntrack maps are LRU_HASH). Robust fix: persist the flow's chosen synthetic port in its FWD_FLOW state and read it back on subsequent packets instead of re-deriving (approach (a) from the round-3 brief) -- idempotent by construction, no re-probe. Test under eviction: commit port_X, free an earlier-probe-index occupant, assert the next packet still resolves to port_X. RELATED: mayor-lrbvo (Phase-4 real-fleet churn/eviction + RSS measurement) is the natural home to validate this under real pressure; the PR already defers general churn/eviction there. This is a narrower, specific instance of that deferral, tracked so it is not lost.

Fix-round proved node-locality makes clean persistence impossible without the unified-flow-table redesign: backend_src_port is decided+re-read on the BACKEND node (try_geneve_decap_forward), FWD_MAIN/FWD_PENDING are ingress-node-only, BPF maps are per-node. title: servicelb-ebpf: uplink parse hard-codes Ethernet L2 (ETH_HLEN=14) -- silently no-ops on L3-only uplinks (WireGuard/overlay)

title: feat(servicelb): expose flow-table traffic-pattern metrics as observability (not a resize control loop)
description:
Expose flow-table traffic-pattern metrics from the dataplane as observability
the loader can read and publish, so operators can right-size the fixed map
ceiling and get alarmed when a node runs hot -- explicitly NOT to drive a
runtime resize control loop (see aie31.11 for why that is declined).

Why observability, not control. A BPF map has no live element count
(confirmed: bpf_map_info carries max_entries but no current-count field), and
LRU eviction is silent, so an accurate live occupancy for an LRU map is
expensive to obtain (full-map iteration) or drifts (a self-maintained counter
cannot be decremented on eviction). What is cheap to expose is a small set of
pressure proxies the datapath can maintain in a PERCPU_ARRAY counter map:

- new-flow inserts per interval (forward-path insert of a previously-absent
  key)
- churn: inserts of a key that was recently evicted, the real "table too
  small" signal
- optionally, high-water concurrent-flow estimate

The loader samples the counter map periodically -- the same shape as the
existing scripts/servicelb/sample-ebpf-memory.sh sampler -- and publishes it
alongside the map-memory and loader-RSS CSVs.

Uses:
1. Right-size the fixed max_entries per node at the NEXT load, feeding the
   load-time configurability knob rather than a reactive swap.
2. Alarm when churn indicates a node is thrashing its conntrack table, which
   is the legitimate-traffic face of the admission-control concern in
   aie31.11 (a burst of new flows evicting established ones).

Cost caveat: the churn proxy adds a compare on the hot path, which cuts
against the direct-packet-access work in aie31.13. Measure before committing
to the churn signal specifically; the plain new-flow counter is nearly free.

DONE WHEN: the loader publishes at least a new-flow-rate metric sampled from a
datapath counter map, in the same CSV/observability shape as the existing
sampler, with the hot-path cost measured.

title: design(servicelb): stateless return-path authorization via a Geneve MAC
description:
Investigate replacing FWD_FLOW entirely with a keyed hash carried in the
Geneve option, since that map stores nothing anyone reads.

FWD_FLOW's value is written at servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:238 and never read.
The only consumer, at line 496, discards it and checks existence alone. So it
is not an affinity table at all, it is a return-path authorization table
answering exactly one question: did this node forward this flow? A question
of that shape does not need storage.

Sketch: the ingress node stamps a keyed hash of the flow tuple into the
forward Geneve option, the backend echoes it alongside the VIP echo it
already sends, and the ingress verifies it against the reconstructed tuple on
return. If it holds up, the larger of the two conntrack maps disappears along
with its eviction behaviour and its flush-attack surface.

Open questions that decide it:

- Needs a per-node secret plus a coarse epoch in the MAC input to bound
  replay of a captured return.
- No HMAC helper exists in tc-bpf, so it means hand-rolling something like
  SipHash-2-4. Cost is roughly comparable to the hash-map lookup it replaces.
- Value depends on the underlay. Over a WireGuard or Tailscale mesh the
  return path is already authenticated and the MAC adds little; in the plain
  colocated case it is doing real work. All four underlays are in scope, so
  it has to be justified against the weakest one.

Depends on the admission-control decision, which may change what the forward
direction needs to store, and interacts with the unified-table bead, which
assumes both populations still exist.

DONE WHEN: a written go or no-go exists, with the underlay reasoning recorded.
notes: SUPERSEDE/RE-SCOPE (operator decision on aie31.21, 2026-09-07): Option A keeps FWD_FLOW as the per-flow affinity store, so aie31.20's premise (FWD_FLOW stores nothing anyone reads -> eliminate it) is now FALSE. Map-elimination is DEAD. Re-scope aie31.20 to 'return-path authorization via a stateless Geneve MAC' ONLY (replacing the main.rs:514 existence-check), keeping the map for affinity -- or supersede if not pursued. Not MVP-blocking.
close_reason: NO-GO (operator decision 2026-09-10). Per-packet cost is ~a wash: no HMAC helper in tc-bpf means hand-rolling SipHash-2-4, whose cost is roughly the LRU_HASH lookup it would replace. The original benefit (eliminate the larger conntrack map + its eviction/flush-attack surface) DIED when the 2026-09-07 aie31.21 Option-A decision kept the map for affinity -- the MAC no longer removes the map, only makes the return leg stateless for auth. And it is redundant over beep's WireGuard cross-node underlay (return path already cryptographically authenticated); the bead required justifying against the weakest underlay, which is exactly where it adds least. DONE-WHEN satisfied: written no-go with underlay reasoning recorded.

Three contained cleanups in the backend port-remap path, all in the same
code, all covered by the existing common-crate tests.

1. Compare occupant identity as raw scalars. servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:367
   and :387 map each occupant through ipv4_mapped_v6 purely so it can be
   compared. The mapping is injective, so comparing the raw address, port,
   and client port is exactly equivalent and turns a 20-byte comparison into
   an 8-byte one, once per probe iteration.

2. Drop the dead high-half XOR in synthetic_port_seed,
   servicelb-common/src/lib.rs:214. It mixes in front_ip bytes 0 through 4,
   which are always zero for an IPv4-mapped address by construction, so the
   term contributes nothing.

3. Hoist the candidate key build out of the probe loop,
   servicelb-ebpf/src/main.rs:384. Only two bytes change per candidate, but
   the buffer's address escapes into bpf_map_lookup_elem, so the compiler
   cannot hoist it and must re-materialize all 37 bytes each iteration. With
   a constant trip count of 16 the loop very likely fully unrolls, putting 16
   copies of a 37-byte stack build into program text.

Calibration: steady-state per-packet cost here is low, because a remapped
flow re-finds its own committed port on the first probe. Treat this as
program size and stack headroom rather than throughput. The merged
geneve_ingress already carries several 37-byte key buffers against a 512-byte
BPF stack limit.

DONE WHEN: the common-crate tests still pass and the compiled program's
instruction count drops.
